answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independently verified work fails or collusion is proven. Reputation attaches to the staked vertex, not a freely chosen name, so creating a thousand identities does not create a thousand trusted workers. The attacker must tie up real capital in every account and risks losing it; yarrow ratings or a vast ocean of fabricated profiles cannot bypass that cost.
